title: "Viash and Viash Hub"
description: "How components are built, containerized, tested, and published."

OpenPipeline is underpinned by two tools: **Viash**, which is used to create each component, and **Viash Hub**, the platform that builds, tests and publishes them.

## Viash: config + script → component

**[Viash](https://viash.io)** turns a config (`config.vsh.yaml`) plus a script into a self-contained component.
From these two files it generates:

- A **command-line interface**, parsing and injecting the declared arguments into the script
- A **Docker image** pinning the component's exact dependencies
- A **Nextflow (VDSL3) module** that can be chained into a workflow

Viash separates a component's **logic** (a script in Python, R, or Bash) from its **execution environment** (the container) and its **orchestration layer** (Nextflow).

## Language independence

Viash components can be written in whichever language is most suitable for that task.
A component that performs statistical testing might use R, one that trains a machine learning model might use Python and one that runs a command line tool might use Bash.
Whichever language is used, the config is defined in the same way.
This means arguments can be defined consistently across components and avoids needing to write repetitive boilerplate code.
Language independence is supported by the environment defined for each component, enabling the creation of the correct environment for each language and allowing components from the same language to have conflicting dependencies.
The independent, language-agnostic components created by Viash allow OpenPipeline to take advantage of the strengths of different ecosystems when building unified workflows.

## The build step

At build time, Viash performs several steps
From the config and script, it creates an executable that can be run locally as well as a compiled Nextflow module
At the same time, it builds the matching container with the environment the script runs in.
The created Nextflow modules can be run directly or included as dependencies in workflow components that chain them into pipelines.
The final Nextflow workflows can be run locally, on an HPC cluster or in the cloud.

## Viash Hub: build, test, publish

**[Viash Hub](https://www.viash-hub.com)** is the platform used by OpenPipeline to build and host Viash components.
When new versions of OpenPipeline packages are ready, Viash Hub builds the components and containers, runs the component and workflow tests and publishes the package to a versioned catalogue.
From the catalog you can browse components, read their parameters, and launch workflows.
The same component and workflow documentation is available in the [reference](../reference/index.qmd) which links to the matching Viash Hub catalogue pages.
